When examining protein-coding genes only (n = 19,942), the Pearson correlation coefficient between gene length and gene expression (per-gene mean of the 723 batch-corrected read counts, zero-expression genes kept) is r ≈ 0.050 (0.050383). This is a very weak positive correlation, but statistically significant (p ≈ 1.09e-12).

Sensitivities (as flagged):
- Median reduction across samples (keep zeros): r ≈ 0.0489 (n = 19,942).
- Drop the 645 zero-expression genes (mean reduction): r ≈ 0.0460 (n = 19,297).

Conclusion: the correlation is weak/positive and robust to the method choices; the primary answer is r ≈ 0.05.
